title: The room he did see
logline: The last page of the sequence in the book: the garage from the doorway, drawn exactly the way the invented rooms were — flat, careful, furnished one object at a time — as if he'd never seen it either. The lamp on. The pup's bed. The boxes.

panels.composition: The garage from its doorway drawn in the same flat careful manner as an invented room: the drafting table, the lamp lit, the dog's bed with a small three-legged dog in it, the wall of numbered boxes, the window with the alley.

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no panel borders, spare knowing ink line with economy, muted ochre and slate blue and sea-foam green washes, a garage studio seen from its doorway drawn flat and careful like a room from a postcard with a drafting table, a lit lamp, a small three-legged dog in a bed, a wall of numbered boxes and a window onto an alley, no words legible

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards

notes: His own room, drawn as if invented.
